answer: Submissions that land within 205 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The ferrous detector writes to shale, and lagoon exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 30 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
